answer: Reputation ripple ledger.** Each identity builds a history of accepted contributions; rewards flow retroactively to prior contributors when downstream work succeeds, so a fresh clone starts with zero incoming ripple and earns nothing until it accrues its own verified history. Cloning thus costs the attacker every foregone nectar of accumulated rewards plus the plume of duplicated effort needed to rebuild standing from scratch, making honest continuation strictly cheaper than spinning up parallel identities.
